approved: Treasury Laws Amendment (Reuniting More Superannuation) Bill 2020
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would close so-called eligible rollover funds by June 2021 and move their money to the Tax Office.
Superannuation accounts held in these funds would be transferred to the Commissioner, who could then match them with a member's active account.
By June 2020, all accounts under $6,000 in these funds must be sent to the Tax Office, and all remaining accounts by June 2021.
Requires eligible rollover funds to transfer all account balances to the Tax Office by specified dates.
Allows the Tax Office Commissioner to proactively reunite transferred amounts with a member's active account.
Stops superannuation funds and retirement savings account providers from depositing new money into eligible rollover funds.
People with superannuation in eligible rollover funds, superannuation funds and retirement savings account providers.

The majority voted against an amendment to the usual second reading motion "*that the bill be read for a [second time](https://www.peo.gov.au/understand-our-parliament/how-parliament-works/bills-and-laws/making-a-law-in-the-australian-parliament/)*" (parliamentary jargon for agreeing with the main idea of the bill). This means it failed. ### Amendment text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House:* > > *(1) notes that Labor created Australia’s superannuation system so that every Australian can have dignity in retirement;* > > *(2) criticises Government members who would see Australia’s world class superannuation system become voluntary for working class Australians; and* > > *(3) further notes that too many Australians retire without adequate retirement savings, which is why our superannuation system needs to be strengthened and protected, not undermined".*

The speaker supported the bill to close eligible rollover funds by 30 June 2021 and transfer lost accounts to the Australian Taxation Office, and moved a second reading amendment criticising government and backbench proposals to weaken the superannuation system, noting that politicians receive a 15% contribution rate while other workers receive 9.5% (rising to 12%).

The speaker argued that the Treasury Laws Amendment (Reuniting More Superannuation) Bill 2020 should close eligible rollover funds (ERFs) to protect retirement savings, citing that the ATO has reunited 2.13 million accounts worth $2.8 billion since 2018. The bill requires all ERF accounts under $6,000 to be transferred to the ATO by 30 June 2020 and all remaining accounts by 30 June 2021, with the speaker accusing some super funds of transferring accounts to ERFs to circumvent reforms and charge more fees.

The speaker supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (Reuniting More Superannuation) Bill 2020 and a second reading amendment by the shadow minister for financial services, criticising the government for undermining compulsory superannuation. The bill facilitates closure of eligible rollover funds by 30 June 2021, implementing a Productivity Commission recommendation, and the ATO has reunited over 2.1 million lost superannuation accounts.

The Treasury Laws Amendment (Reuniting More Superannuation) Bill 2020 closes loopholes that allowed superannuation funds to reactivate low-balance inactive accounts via eligible rollover funds to charge additional fees, and the compulsory superannuation guarantee increase suppresses wage growth—a link denied by the opposition, as supported by the Grattan Institute and the Reserve Bank governor.

The government opposed the opposition's second reading amendment and supported the Treasury Laws Amendment (Reuniting More Superannuation) Bill 2020, which will remove all eligible rollover funds from the superannuation system by 30 June 2021, building on the Protecting Your Super reforms and implementing Productivity Commission recommendation 5.
